source_review.notes: Retrieved and reviewed the primary ARIES paper and IBM publication record; current PostgreSQL 18 WAL, checkpoint, recovery, record-reader, and record-format sources; current MySQL 8.4 redo, undo, and recovery documentation; current SQLite atomic-commit and WAL documentation; and current SQL Server transaction-log documentation. Cross-engine claims distinguish ARIES-style physical undo, MVCC visibility, rollback journals, redo logs, and product-specific current behavior.

evidence: Checked force/no-force, steal/no-steal, winner, loser, prepared, before-image, after-image, redo, undo, CLR, prevLSN, undoNextLSN, pageLSN, and repeat-history definitions.
Checked update-record notation and winner/loser sets remain distinct from transaction visibility and physical page presence.
Checked idempotence, restartability, database compensation, business compensation, and external exactly-once behavior are not conflated.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Every recovery operation is scoped to a record type, identity/generation, outcome, history, and algorithm rather than an unqualified inverse.

evidence: Independently classified T1 as winner and T2 as loser from a durable prefix ending at 50.
Independently reconstructed repeat-history A=130/B=65, compensation A=130/B=70, and final A=130/B=50.
Independently verified T2 reverse chain 50,20, CLR undoNextLSN 20, winner preservation, loser removal, and all four buffer-policy matrix results.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Independent finite-schedule results are retained in artifacts/reviews/DBE-074/independent-recomputation.txt and do not import the chapter executable.

evidence: Derived redo need from no-force and undo need from steal under the stated page-policy model.
Derived record coverage and page applicability from WAL, page identity/generation/integrity, pageLSN, and record-specific predicates.
Derived restartable undo from durable CLR-before-page ordering, redoable compensation, non-undoable CLR semantics, and decreasing undoNextLSN.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The derivations remain conditional on a verified prefix, sufficient record information, valid outcome evidence, retained history, and correct recovery code.

evidence: Reviewed crashes before and after update, commit, abort, prepare, redo, CLR append/flush, compensated page write, completion, and another recovery restart.

Reviewed repeated page updates, interleaved losers, savepoints, prepared transactions, nested/system actions, page reuse, corrupt chains, cycles, unknown types, hostile lengths, torn pages, and ENOSPC during rollback.
Reviewed external effects, sensitive before/after values, key unavailability, incompatible record readers, force-recovery modes, and unsafe downgrade.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Corrupt, unknown, wrong-generation, unbounded, or in-doubt state fails closed instead of being guessed or skipped.

evidence: Checked durable recovery information precedes every dependent escaped page and durable commit evidence governs winner classification.
Checked redo preserves required physical history and undo targets only loser-owned effects while preserving committed/system work.
Checked every escaped compensation is preceded by its CLR and every CLR redirects rather than becoming an undo target.
invariant_checking.notes: Information sufficiency, redo safety, undo safety, restartability, and atomic outcome are reviewed as separate invariants.

evidence: Reviewed the four buffer-policy cases against reachable old-winner and escaped-loser page states.
Reviewed repeat-history preconditions, pageLSN skip logic, backward transaction chains, CLR WAL ordering, and monotone undo progress line by line.
Reviewed why prepared transactions, MVCC remnants, structural actions, and external side effects require policies outside ordinary loser physical undo.
proof_review.notes: No recovery claim exceeds the admitted crash, integrity, persistence, version, resource-progress, or database boundary assumptions.

evidence: The executable is explicitly a finite schedule and excludes concurrency, codecs, latches, storage, checkpoints, prepare, and external effects.
ARIES theory, general design alternatives, and PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, and SQL Server behaviors are separately labeled.
Formal invariants, exact finite execution, fuzzing, model checking, storage fault tests, restore drills, and production observation are distinguished.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The chapter does not present one product decomposition as a universal undo/redo architecture.

evidence: Repository verification passed one standard-library Python snippet with exact sixteen-line stdout, empty stderr, zero exit status, and recorded toolchain metadata.
Independent reconstruction reproduced winner/loser classification, redo state, undo order, CLR state, restart state, final state, and policy matrix.
Thirteen retained source artifacts were file-type checked, and structural validation checked every local link and required section/example/exercise shape.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No live database rollback, crash recovery, prepared transaction, page corruption, storage/power fault, external payment, restore, security assessment, or production workload was exercised.

conceptual_review.notes: Correction review rechecked record information, buffer policies, redo guards, semantic undo, outcome classification, repeat history, transaction chains, CLRs, partial rollback, MVCC history, structural actions, external boundaries, testing, operations, security, and compatibility. Revised examples derive outcomes from explicit page values, transaction histories, identity assumptions, or resource frontiers and defer the complete ARIES pass derivation to DBE-076.

practitioner_review.notes: Correction review rechecked rollback-space reserve, long-transaction debt, prepared-state handling, hostile parsing, page generations, post-recovery oracles, progress and lock observability, service admission during recovery, force-recovery limitations, reader-before-writer rollout, canary crash tests, and format-aware rollback.

pedagogical_review.notes: The corrected chapter derives undo/redo needs from the policy matrix, executes repeat history and crash-during-undo, covers sixteen distinct misconceptions, and gives all ten examples concrete state traces, assumption boundaries, and explicit conclusions. Five exercises still advance from policy retrieval to payment-system transfer with complete answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/official-source review, mathematical review, executable-snippet verification, conceptual review, practitioner review, and pedagogical review only; no external database-recovery researcher, engine maintainer, storage engineer, distributed-transaction specialist, SRE, security reviewer, payment-domain reviewer, or educator review is claimed. The evidence does not prove a live engine, storage stack, rollback implementation, prepared-transaction protocol, MVCC purge, external workflow, recovery time, security posture, performance, or deployment fitness.
